groups.title: Soft capsule (E92700ACS)
groups.efficacy: This is an over-the-counter medicine used to supply vitamins A, D, E, B1, B2, B6 and C in physical tiredness, in pregnancy and breast-feeding, when strength is reduced during or after an illness, during growth and in later life; for the relief of dryness of the eyes and for night blindness; for poor growth of the bones and teeth and the prevention of rickets; for the prevention and treatment of iron deficiency anaemia; and to supply zinc.
groups.usage: Those aged 12 years and over and adults: take 1 capsule at a time, 1 time in 1 day.
groups.caution:
If a pregnant woman takes 5,000 IU or more of vitamin A in 1 day it can cause birth defects. Women in the first 3 months of pregnancy, or who may be pregnant, must not take it.
Keep it out of the reach of children. Iron-containing preparations can cause fatal poisoning if a child aged 6 years or under accidentally takes too much.

Do not take this medicine if you have a high calcium level in the blood, sarcoidosis (a generalised inflammatory disease of unknown cause) or kidney disease; if you have hypersensitivity to this medicine; if the user is a baby under 12 months of age; if you have a high potassium level in the blood, haemochromatosis (a disease in which iron is deposited in the liver and pancreas because of abnormal iron metabolism), haemosiderosis, anaemia that is not due to iron deficiency, kidney stones or severe kidney failure; or if you have hypersensitivity to soya-bean oil or have had an allergic reaction to it, or hypersensitivity to soya or peanut.
Before taking this medicine, consult a doctor or pharmacist if you have high oxalate levels in the urine; if you are pregnant, may be pregnant or are breast-feeding; if the user is a premature baby or an infant; if you have a gastrointestinal disease such as peptic ulcer, chronic ulcerative colitis or regional colitis; if you have impaired heart or circulatory function, kidney disorder or a low protein level in the blood; if you have gallbladder disease, liver disease, acute or chronic bronchitis, fluid in the lungs, alkalosis, peptic ulcer, diabetes, or gout or kidney stones, or have had kidney stones; if you have a disorder of fat metabolism such as hyperlipoproteinaemia, diabetic hyperlipidaemia or pancreatitis, or fat emulsions must be given to you with care; if you have hypersensitivity to Food Yellow No. 5 or Sunset Yellow FCF or have had an allergic reaction to them; or if fat overload is a concern for you.
If you have a tendency to thrombosis, or if you are short of folic acid, stop taking it immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist.
If there is no improvement in symptoms after about 1 month of use, stop taking it immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist.
Keep to the stated dosage and schedule.
The vitamin A in this medicine is supplied in sufficient amounts by a normal diet, so as a supplement do not go above 5,000 IU in 1 day.
It can interfere with the detection of sugar in urine tests and can turn the urine yellow, so it may affect laboratory test results.

Do not take it together with phosphates, calcium salts, oral tetracycline preparations, antacids or levodopa.
Consult a doctor or pharmacist if you take it together with an oral contraceptive containing oestrogen, anti-aldosterone medicines, triamterene or intravenous lipid preparations.
Avoid tea containing tannin, such as green tea and black tea, during the period of use and just before and after a dose.

If nausea, vomiting, itching, dry and rough skin, painful swelling of the joints, diarrhoea, stomach discomfort, constipation, rash, reddening, loose stools, hives, a photosensitivity reaction, abdominal or stomach pain, cramps, fever, coma, an allergic reaction, angioedema, joint pain, a rise in eosinophils, iodine poisoning, a high potassium level, wind, stomach pain, dermatitis, an unpleasant smell of sweat or breath, hair loss, impatience, gastrointestinal disturbance, digestive disturbance, upper abdominal pain, low blood pressure or fluid in the lungs occurs, or if a period comes earlier than expected, the bleeding gradually becomes heavier, or bleeding lasts a long time, stop taking it immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist.

summaryTable.What it is for: Supply of vitamins A, D, E, B1, B2, B6 and C and of zinc, relief of dry eyes and night blindness, bone and tooth growth, and iron deficiency anaemia

summaryTable.Ask the pharmacist: Ask the pharmacist in the store first if any of the cautions above apply to you.

groups.title: Soft capsule (E30600ACS)
groups.efficacy: This is an over-the-counter medicine used for the relief of headache, toothache, pain after a tooth extraction, sore throat, earache, joint pain, neuralgia, back pain, muscle pain, stiff shoulders, bruising pain, fracture pain, sprain pain, menstrual pain (period pain) and pain from injury, and to bring down fever when there are chills (feeling cold and shivering) and a raised temperature.
groups.usage: Adults and those aged 15 years and over: take 1 capsule at a time, 1 to 3 times in 1 day, avoiding an empty stomach. Leave an interval of at least 4 hours between doses.
groups.caution:
If you regularly drink three or more glasses of alcohol every day, consult a doctor or pharmacist before taking this medicine or any other antipyretic analgesic. It may cause gastrointestinal bleeding.
People with uncontrolled high blood pressure, congestive heart failure, established ischaemic heart disease, peripheral arterial disease or cerebrovascular disease should use ibuprofen only after careful consideration and should avoid high-dose ibuprofen (2,400 mg in 1 day). People with cardiovascular risk factors (for example high blood pressure, high blood fats, diabetes, smoking) who need high-dose ibuprofen (2,400 mg in 1 day) should consider carefully before starting long-term treatment. Clinical studies have shown that high-dose ibuprofen (2,400 mg in 1 day) may slightly increase the risk of arterial thrombotic events (myocardial infarction or stroke).

Do not take this medicine if you have hypersensitivity to it, if you have had asthma with this medicine or with another antipyretic analgesic or cold medicine, or if the user is an infant under 3 months of age.
Before taking this medicine, consult a doctor or pharmacist if the user is an infant or a child under 15 years of age who has, or is suspected of having, chickenpox or influenza; if you have an allergic constitution or have had allergic symptoms (fever, rash, joint pain, asthma, itching and the like); if you have liver disease, kidney disease, thyroid disease, diabetes or high blood pressure; if you are physically weak or have a high fever; if you are pregnant, may be pregnant or are breast-feeding; if you are an older person; if you have heartburn, stomach discomfort, stomach pain or another stomach problem that lasts or comes back, or an ulcer or a bleeding problem; if you have lost a lot of body fluid through vomiting and diarrhoea or are unable to take fluid in; if you have hypersensitivity to Food Yellow No. 5 or have had it; or if the user is a child under 2 years of age.
Keep to the stated dosage and schedule.
If there is no improvement in symptoms after 5 or 6 doses, stop taking it immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist.

Do not take it together with other antipyretic analgesics, cold medicines or sedatives.
Consult a doctor or pharmacist if you take it together with medicines for diabetes, gout or arthritis, anticoagulants, steroids, diuretics or low-dose aspirin.
Do not drink alcohol while you are taking it.

If rash or reddening, itching, nausea or vomiting, loss of appetite, constipation, stomach pain, bleeding from the digestive tract, stomach discomfort, dizziness or oedema occurs, or rarely shock (hives, swelling and tightness of the chest immediately after a dose, together with pallor, cold hands and feet, cold sweat and difficulty breathing), Stevens-Johnson syndrome, toxic epidermal necrolysis (Lyell's syndrome — severe symptoms with high fever, and a rash or reddening with burn-like blisters, on the skin of the whole body and on the mucous membranes of the mouth or eyes), asthma, or very rarely erythema multiforme, exfoliative dermatitis, a photosensitivity reaction of unknown frequency, drug reaction with eosinophilia and systemic symptoms (DRESS syndrome) or acute generalised exanthematous pustulosis, stop taking it immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist.

summaryTable.What it is for: Headache, toothache and pain after tooth extraction, sore throat, earache, joint, nerve, back and muscle pain, stiff shoulders, injury pain and period pain, and fever

groups.title: Capsule (433200ACH)
groups.efficacy: This is an over-the-counter medicine used for the relief of the various symptoms of a cold (runny nose, blocked nose, sneezing, sore throat, cough, phlegm, chills (feeling cold and shivering), fever, headache, joint pain, muscle pain).
groups.usage: Those aged 8 years and over but under 11 years: take 1 capsule at a time. Adults and those aged 15 years and over: take 2 capsules at a time. Take it 3 times in 1 day, 30 minutes after meals.
groups.caution:
If you regularly drink three or more glasses of alcohol every day, consult a doctor or pharmacist before taking this medicine or any other antipyretic analgesic. It may cause liver damage.
Very rarely, serious skin reactions that can be fatal — acute generalised exanthematous pustulosis, Stevens-Johnson syndrome and toxic epidermal necrolysis — have been reported; if a skin rash or another sign of hypersensitivity appears after a dose of this medicine, stop taking it at once.
Do not go above the maximum daily amount of acetaminophen (4,000 mg). It may cause liver damage. Do not take it together with other products containing acetaminophen.
If a severe skin reaction such as acute generalised exanthematous pustulosis occurs, stop taking it and consult a doctor or pharmacist.

Do not take this medicine if you have hypersensitivity to it or have had it, if you have had asthma when taking another antipyretic analgesic or a cold medicine, if the user is a child under 2 years of age, if you have severe or uncontrolled high blood pressure, or if you have severe acute or chronic kidney disease or kidney failure.
Before taking this medicine, consult a doctor or pharmacist if the user is an infant or a child under 15 years of age who has, or is suspected of having, chickenpox or influenza; if symptoms of ischaemic colitis (sudden abdominal pain, rectal bleeding and the like) appear in connection with the pseudoephedrine component; if you have an allergic constitution or have had allergic symptoms caused by a medicine (for example fever, rash, joint pain, asthma, itching); if you have liver disease, kidney disease, heart disease, thyroid disease, diabetes, high blood pressure, oedema, gastric or duodenal ulcer, glaucoma (for example eye pain, blurred vision) or difficulty passing urine; if you are an older person, physically weak or have a high fever; if you have heartburn, stomach discomfort, stomach pain or another stomach problem that lasts or comes back, or an ulcer or a bleeding problem; if you are pregnant, may be pregnant or are breast-feeding; or if you smoke, or have asthma, chronic bronchitis, emphysema, a cough with a lot of phlegm, a cough lasting or coming back for more than 1 week, a chronic cough, or a cough with fever, rash or a persistent headache.
If there is no improvement in symptoms after 5 or 6 doses, stop taking it immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist.
Keep to the stated dosage and schedule.
When it is given to a child, give it under the guidance and supervision of a guardian.
Drowsiness may occur after a dose, so be careful when driving or operating machinery.

Do not take it together with cough and expectorant medicines, other cold medicines, antipyretic analgesics, sedatives, or oral medicines containing antihistamines (oral medicines for rhinitis, travel sickness medicines, allergy medicines).
Do not take this medicine if you are taking an MAO inhibitor (antidepressant, antipsychotic, mood stabiliser, anti-Parkinson medicine and the like) or stopped taking one within the last 2 weeks.
Consult a doctor or pharmacist if you take it together with medicines for diabetes, gout or arthritis, anticoagulants, steroids, barbiturates, tricyclic antidepressants, alcohol, preparations containing potassium, preparations containing liquorice, preparations containing glycyrrhizic acid or its salts, loop diuretics (furosemide, etacrynic acid), thiazide diuretics (trichlormethiazide) or flucloxacillin.
Do not drink alcohol while you are taking it.

If rash or reddening, itching, nausea or vomiting, loss of appetite, constipation, swelling, difficulty passing urine, thirst (persistent or severe), dizziness, anxiety, tremor, insomnia or high anion gap metabolic acidosis occurs, or rarely shock (hives, swelling and tightness of the chest immediately after a dose, together with pallor, cold hands and feet, cold sweat and difficulty breathing), Stevens-Johnson syndrome, toxic epidermal necrolysis (severe symptoms with high fever, and a rash or reddening with burn-like blisters), acute generalised exanthematous pustulosis, a severe skin reaction such as fever, erythema and many small pustules, asthma, generalised weakness, jaundice, interstitial pneumonia (cough with shortness of breath, difficulty breathing and fever), a fall in the amount of urine with swelling of the face, hands and feet, heavy eyelids, stiff hands, a rise in blood pressure or headache, muscle disease (weakness, cramps of the limbs, paralysis), or symptoms of reversible posterior encephalopathy syndrome and reversible cerebral vasoconstriction syndrome (a sudden severe headache, thunderclap headache, nausea, vomiting, confusion, seizures, visual disturbance), stop taking it immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist.

groups.title: Tablet (110401ATB)
groups.efficacy: This is an over-the-counter medicine used for the prevention and treatment of scurvy; for wasting conditions in which the requirement for vitamin C is increased, such as pregnancy, breast-feeding, reduced strength during and after an illness and physical tiredness; for capillary bleeding such as bleeding gums, nosebleeds and blood in the urine; for pigmentation caused by sunlight or skin disease (melasma, freckles); and for cases such as poor absorption where a lack of vitamin C is thought to be involved.
groups.usage: Adults: take 1/2 to 1 tablet (500 to 1000 mg), 1 time in 1 day or divided into several doses. Take it with plenty of water, and do not lie down straight after a dose.
groups.caution:
Do not take this medicine if you have hypersensitivity to it, high oxalate levels in the urine, thalassaemia, gout, cystinuria, glucose-6-phosphate dehydrogenase (G6PD) deficiency, or oxalate kidney stones (when 1 g or more is taken in 1 day).
Before taking this medicine, consult a doctor or pharmacist if you are pregnant or breast-feeding, if you have oxalate kidney stones, if you smoke, or if you drink alcohol regularly.
Keep to the stated dosage and schedule.
When it is given to a child, give it under the guidance and supervision of a guardian.
If there is no improvement in symptoms after about 1 month of use, stop taking it immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist.
It can interfere with the detection of sugar in urine tests.

Avoid drinking or smoking to excess.
Consult a doctor or pharmacist if you take it together with oral anticoagulants (coumarin medicines), salicylates, aspirin, iron preparations, phenytoin and some antiepileptic medicines, oral contraceptives containing oestrogen, tetracycline antibiotics, fluphenazine, orlistat, barbiturate derivatives or corticosteroids.

If nausea, vomiting, diarrhoea, heartburn, facial flushing, headache or insomnia occurs, stop taking it immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist.

groups.title: Tablet (A03000ATB)
groups.efficacy: This is an over-the-counter medicine used as an aid to weight loss by reducing the amount of food taken.
groups.usage: Take 2 tablets at a time, 3 times in 1 day, before meals; if needed, a further 2 tablets may be taken before going to bed. It is best to take it with plenty of water. It is recommended that the recommended amount be taken for at least 3 to 4 weeks.
groups.caution:
Do not take this medicine if you have hypersensitivity to it, or if the user is an infant or a child.
Before taking this medicine, consult a doctor or pharmacist if you are pregnant or breast-feeding, or if you have a digestive disorder.
Keep to the stated dosage and schedule.
If there is no improvement in symptoms after 1 month or more of use, stop taking it immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist.

It is best not to take it at the same time as other medicines; if you do, it is recommended that you leave an interval of 30 minutes to 1 hour between them.

If a feeling of abdominal bloating, nausea, constipation or diarrhoea occurs, stop taking it immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist.

groups.usage: Adults: take 1 to 2 capsules at a time, 3 times in 1 day, 30 minutes before meals.
groups.caution:
Do not take this medicine during the first 3 months of pregnancy.
Before taking this medicine, consult a doctor or pharmacist if you are pregnant or breast-feeding.

Consult a doctor or pharmacist if you take it together with oral anticoagulants or with medicines that are broken down and excreted by the liver.

Belching, nausea, vomiting and similar symptoms may occur.

summaryTable.What it is for: Gallstone disease, and prevention of stones coming back after gallstone surgery
summaryTable.Choosing a product: Products with the same generic-name code (B06800ACS) share the same ingredient, strength and dosage form. Check the ingredient and strength rather than the brand name.
summaryTable.Ask the pharmacist: Ask the pharmacist in the store first if any of the cautions above apply to you.
